panels.label: Head feedback
panels.note: Recovered the edge and passed the five-second hold.
panels.detail: The turquoise trace is measured lean. The line marks the target.

panels.label: Head held still
panels.setup: Same release angle and neutral starting head
panels.detail: Both runs use the same waist target and bounded battery servos.

timeline.title: Two ways an attempted catch can end

panels.label: 24° release
panels.note: Fell inward and finished on its foot.
panels.detail: A physical joint limit was reached during this failed catch.

panels.label: 40° release
panels.note: The torso hit the floor 0.30 seconds after release.
panels.detail: The simulation continued through the joint warning and landing.

timeline.title: Can Reachy roll while lying on its side?

panels.label: Head moving
panels.setup: Four head cycles at 1 Hz, left side down
panels.note: The torso rolled through a 39.9° arc.
panels.detail: 9.7 mm minimum sampled head clearance during and after the stroke.

panels.label: Head held still
panels.setup: Identical head pose and eight-second settling period
panels.detail: The floor-contact check includes lenses and both antennas.

timeline.title: Where the larger motion loses clearance

panels.label: Head-clear stroke
panels.setup: Four head cycles at 1 Hz, left side down
panels.note: Most of the measured rotation reversed.
panels.detail: Torso support continued throughout all four cycles and settling.

panels.label: Larger head stroke
panels.setup: Same setup, twice the head excursion
panels.note: The head first touched the floor at 10.28 s.
panels.detail: The resulting half-turn includes head contact with the floor.
